model.architecture: IBM Granite 4.0-h hybrid: 28 Mamba2 selective-scan blocks interleaved with 4 grouped-query attention blocks; per-layer conv + SSM recurrent state instead of a growing KV cache

variants.quantization: fp16 weights (float-casting on linears + embedding; convs and the SSM stay fp32)

measured.source: S7 Android backfill: same-device CPU control - identical binary, prompt file and flags, only --backend differs; 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); the GPU path does not run for this file on this handset, so this row has no GPU counterpart

known_issues: CPU only, for two independent reasons. The same rank-5/6 scan graph as _int8 above, and - even after that is rewritten - float-casting EMBEDDING_LOOKUP leaves empty quantization params plus a DEQUANTIZE the delegate will not take (3326 of 3536 ops, engine refused). There is no fp16 GPU variant; use _int8_gpu.
The CPU runtime unpacks fp16 weights to fp32 in RAM (~3.7 GB peak on iPhone vs ~2.1 GB for int8) - treat fp16 as the desktop/quality variant.

variants.quantization: int8 dynamic weight-only (linears + embedding; convs and the SSM stay float)

measured.source: S7 Android backfill: same-device CPU control - identical binary, prompt file and flags, only --backend differs; 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); the GPU path does not run for this file on this handset, so this row has no GPU counterpart

S7 Android backfill: same-device CPU control - identical binary, prompt file and flags, only --backend differs; 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); the GPU path does not run for this file on this handset, so this row has no GPU counterpart

known_issues: Cannot create a GPU engine: this export writes the Mamba2 SSD contractions as broadcast-multiply-reduce, materialising rank-5 and rank-6 intermediates that every mobile GPU delegate refuses. On a Galaxy S26 the delegate takes 109 of 3673 ops and the runtime refuses the partial split - use the _int8_gpu file for the same weights on GPU.
Engine state reuse: chat-templated lengths 33-37 (LiteRT-LM#3165); a fresh Engine per conversation is clean.

variants.quantization: int8 dynamic weight-only (linears + embedding; convs and the SSM stay float), fp32 activations declared

recommended.reason: measured on one Galaxy S26 with one binary (S5 gate 2026-08-27, 205-token prompt): CPU decodes 97.6 tok/s against the GPU's 48.8, and peaks at 1105 MB against 2131 MB; the GPU wins only prefill (486.5 vs 305.6 tok/s). Same-device CPU control taken, so this is a measured win for CPU on decode and memory; choose gpu only for prompt-heavy, short-output work. This file (not the _int8 sibling, which cannot create a GPU engine) is the one both backends were measured on

measured on one Pixel 8a with one binary (S7 Android backfill 2026-09-07, 205-token prompt, 2 cold runs per backend, cooled before each run): cpu decodes 40.42 tok/s against gpu's 20.54 (2.0x), prefill 102.8-110.6 vs 180.4 tok/s, peak 1081 vs 4307 MB, engine init 3.1 vs 37.3 s. Same-device GPU control taken - a measured win for cpu on decode. Same direction as the flagship recommendation on the Galaxy S26 (cpu, 2.0x there). The GPU path runs fully delegated (all 12 subgraphs on LiteRT GPU) and answered the probe, but needs a 37 s engine init and peaks at 4.3 GB on this 7.75 GB phone against 1.1 GB on the CPU; it wins only prefill (180 vs 103-111 tok/s). Ship this file, not the CPU-lineage _int8 sibling, on 8 GB-class Android as well: on this phone's CPU the same weights decode 40 tok/s from this export against 7-9 tok/s from _int8 (row of 2026-09-05)

platform_notes: Requires litert-lm >= 0.15: the hybrid conv/SSM state buffers bind through the ExecutorMetadata section, which the 0.14 engine does not read
The bundle does not prepend a BOS token, matching Granite's official chat template; at 350M scale a prepended <|end_of_text|> measurably degrades greedy answers
On a Galaxy S26 the GPU path wins prefill and loses decode - pick the backend by workload, not by assuming GPU is faster

measured.source: S5 same-device CPU control, identical prompt file and flags; phone already warm from the GPU runs

S7 Android backfill: 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); GPU gate full LITERT_CL delegation (38313 ops across 12 subgraphs), generation verified on the gate prompt; the cpu row of the same date is the same-device control

S7 Android backfill: same-device CPU control - identical binary, prompt file and flags, only --backend differs; 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); same-device control for the gpu row of the same date

known_issues: Engine state reuse, not quantization: reusing one Engine across conversations whose prompts share a growing common prefix can end a reply after a few tokens, on this file at chat-templated lengths 37-41 (LiteRT-LM#3165). A fresh Engine per conversation is clean at every length tested, 35-45.
GPU peak memory is about twice the CPU path's (2131 MB vs 1105 MB on the S26 benchmark).
